title: Stormshield details Trigram campaign impersonating about 50 AI and blockchain brands to deliver infostealers to developers
date_note: Publication date of The Hacker News report.
actor: Overlaps with Kimsuky and Contagious Interview, per Stormshield (technique overlap only)
summary: Stormshield describes Trigram, a campaign impersonating about 50 blockchain and AI brands to trick developers in Europe and the US into running an infostealer. Lures include fake recruiting and a forged commit in the antd-img-crop repository on October 31; the npm package was not affected. Stormshield links it to the UNK_DeadDrop cluster and notes overlap with North Korea-linked groups.
plain: A campaign posing as AI and crypto firms tricks developers into running password-stealing software.
exec: Developer machines hold keys, wallets and .env secrets, so one run of a fake build step can expose company credentials.
action: Treat recruiter and conference lures with caution, do not run build scripts from unverified repositories, and rotate secrets on any machine that did.

validation.note: The Hacker News report read in full on Stormshield's research; the original Stormshield page was not read.

review.note: THN Nov 17: about 50 brands, Oct 31 forged commit, npm unaffected, UNK_DeadDrop and Kimsuky/Contagious Interview overlap wording match; Stormshield original unread.
